newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey threatens military strike on Cyprus missiles.
newsitem.headline: Turkey threatens military strike on Cyprus missiles.

text.p: Turkey is seriously considering staging a military strike if Cyprus goes ahead with plans to deploy Russian anti-aircraft missiles on the divided island, the state-run Anatolian news agency reported on Thursday.
"Ankara is seriously considering an operation against the missile launchers when the time comes if Turkey's warnings to the Greek Cypriot administration are not heeded," the agency said.

Turkey has accused the Cypriot government of trying to change the balance of forces on Cyprus with a deal announced last weekend to buy Russian S-300 surface-to-air missiles that could neutralise Turkish air superiority on the island.
Earlier, Defence Minister Turhan Tayan said that Turkey would use all possible means to halt the missile deployment. It is unclear when the missiles will be delivered.

The Cypriot government says the missiles are defensive. The S-300 air defence missile system is believed to have a range of 150 km (90 miles) and is designed to knock out aircraft and ballistic missiles in flight.

Turkey invaded Cyprus in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup inspired by the military then ruling Athens. Around 30,000 troops are based in north Cyprus, declared a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in 1983 and recognised only by Ankara.
The Greek Cypriot administration in the south is internationally recognised as the island's only government.
The United States is to send an envoy to the island at the weekend to try to reduce tensions between Greeks and Turks.

Washington has criticised Cyprus, saying the missile purchase would introduce a destabilising new military element and complicate peace moves. Former colonial power Britain has also expressed its concern.
